request: Ship the Baseline output style as an installed default. The ASD-STE100 style file at .claude/output-styles/baseline.md already lands in the tarball via the Stage 1 .claude/ rsync, but nothing sets it as the default for a consumer install. Wire outputStyle into src/settings.template.json and .claude/settings.json (tests/template-drift.test.mjs asserts byte parity), drop the now-redundant .claude/settings.local.json entry, pin the style file with a REQUIRED_PATTERNS row in tests/template-payload.test.mjs so it can never silently stop shipping, and amend docs/init/seed.md (§3 directory tree + a new §4.9 Output styles section) plus the CLAUDE.md quick-orientation counts first, per Article I.4 precedence. Shipped style carries two modes only (Engineer, Analyst) — Quirky Mode is deliberately excluded.
novelty_evidence: seed.md §15.5 (CI/secrets posture, slice J2) + tests/template-payload.test.mjs:83-87 + scripts/build-template.sh Stage 2.6. Slice J2 shipped a new payload class (.githooks/, scripts/ci/, .github/branch-protection/) default-on with a CLI opt-out, pinned by REQUIRED_PATTERNS rows and declared in its own seed section. This request repeats that exact shape for .claude/output-styles/. Distribution path already verified: build-template.sh Stage 1 rsyncs .claude/ verbatim with no output-styles exclude, and template-payload.test.mjs ALLOWED_PREFIXES carries the '.claude/' prefix.
track_reason: Heavier than the leanest safe track (tdd-quickfix). Setting outputStyle on by default changes how the assistant speaks in every consumer install — a consumer-facing product default, not a mechanical parameter. The load-bearing fork (default-on with an opt-out lever, per the J2 precedent, versus opt-in) is a human's-call decision under Article XI.12 and belongs at gate A. spec-entry also retains spec-shippability-review, which tdd-quickfix excepts.
